brief.situation: 10:00 in an outpatient neurologic clinic. You are the physical therapist. Mr. Brandt, 71, has had Parkinson disease for 8 years. His referral says 'treadmill training'. His wife says he freezes in doorways, has fallen twice in 3 months, sits most of the day now, coughs when he drinks, and 'seems down'.
handover: He sees his neurologist every 6 months; no speech-language or occupational therapist is involved.
Clinic policy: share findings outside physical therapy scope with the referring neurologist the same day.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

scoring.modelReasoning: Parkinson disease care works best as integrated care: physical therapy alongside neurology, speech-language pathology, occupational therapy and mental health. Behavior-change strategies (a meaningful goal, self-monitoring) raise activity, and telerehabilitation may be used to improve balance. For freezing, use external cueing with gait and task practice, and consider cycling over treadmill walking when fall risk is high or freezing is present.
